messages:
anya: Heads up — onboarding nova-signalspace-7b. After tokenizer conversion we're seeing a subtle rotary-phase shift + kv-cache misalignment on long context tests. Small repro below.

cheng: Ah. Not familiar with 'signalspace' name — is this a head-interleave variant or just a naming quirk from the export?

anya: It's a head-interleave variant. Export came from model-converter v0.9.2. Conversion logs show no errors but generation diverges after ~256 tokens compared to reference.

sam: Can you paste the conversion command and a minimal repro?

anya: Sure — conversion command:```bash
python convert.py --src-format pt --dst-format rwd --model nova-signalspace-7b --tokenizer tok.json --out out_dir
```Repro: feed the prompt "The history of AI shows" with greedy sampling; model diverges past token 260 (seeded).

ciara: Do you see a token-id offset or just phase mismatch? If token ids are off, logits shift; if phase it's rotary alignment.

anya: Logs show kvcache keys not matching when we compare activations between reference FP16 run and our int8 runtime: head 3/24 has shifted phase by ~0.03 radians in scaled sin/cos table. Token ids seem consistent.

cheng: Interesting. Could be an embed projection ordering (signalspace exports headmix as interleaved per-head vs per-block). We had a similar symptom with orion where per-head ordering changed the rotary index mapping.

sam: Quick checks: 1) dump the rotary sin/cos table after conversion and compare elementwise with reference; 2) run a short deterministic forward and diff per-head k/v before and after first attention.

anya: Did both. Attached small diffs inline: "rotary_table_diff_max: 0.032" and "k_cache_shift_index: 1" — looks like a single-index offset in the table alignment relative to head stride.

ciara: That smells like a stride/stride-mismatch during reshape. Are we doing reshape as (num_heads, head_dim) vs (head_dim, num_heads) somewhere?

anya: Converter currently uses reshape: view(-1, n_heads, head_dim). If export assumed head-major layout we need to transpose.

sam: Also check tokenizer special tokens. If BOS/EOS got remapped, some earlier cache priming might shift phase propagation. But your kv index==1 suggests structural, not tokenizer.

cheng: Another possibility: quantization packer applies per-channel scaling then reorders channels for int4 packing. If packing reorders channels, sin/cos alignment breaks unless we apply the same reordering to rotary tables. Did converter apply quant packing before or after permute?

anya: We quantized after conversion (post-convert int4 pipeline). The packer does a channel-major reorder for bitpacking. I will rerun packer with no reordering flag.

deploy-bot: sample-eval-run started: job_id=job_2026_03_21_01

ciara: If removing reordering fixes it, we need to either: A) make the packer preserve logical channel order; or B) apply the same reorder to rotary sin/cos tables and any headwise params (proj weights, bias). Option A is safer.

anya: Quick experiment: re-run packer with --no-reorder. Early result: rotary_table_diff_max -> 7e-6, kv_cache_shift_index -> 0. Deterministic samples now match reference through 1024 tokens.

sam: Nice. So reordering was the culprit. Makes sense: packer was optimizing layout for memory but didn't update metadata about head-channel layout.

cheng: Action items: - sam/eng-ml: add a unit test in converter pipeline that validates sin/cos table roundtrip after pack/quant. - infra: ensure packer exposes metadata describing final channel ordering. - anya: re-run full eval suite and post regression numbers.

anya: On it. First pass eval: small eval through our summarization set shows Rouge-L delta -0.6 pts on int4 with old packer; with --no-reorder it's within noise (±0.1). I'll upload full CSV shortly.

ciara: Also add a smoke test: forward equality of (k_head_i, v_head_i) for first 3 heads between reference and converted on a fixed prompt. That would catch this early.

anya: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: please link the converter PR when ready; might be worth adding a flag to packer to auto-apply reorder to rotary tables to preserve perf option but keep correctness.

anya: Filed ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/ML-8342 — notes + minimal repro.

deploy-bot: sample-eval-run completed: job_id=job_2026_03_21_01, status=success, artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/nova-signalspace/2026-03-21/run1/

anya: Uploaded CSV, summary: int4-oldpacker rougeL=27.4, int4-no-reorder rougeL=28.0, fp16 baseline rougeL=28.1. So no-reorder gets us nearly baseline.

ciara: Great triage. We'll follow up with a small PR to packer to add metadata and unit tests.

cheng: Marking this thread resolved for now. If anyone sees other headwise mismatches ping here.

sam: :white_check_mark:
